summary: GOLDEN LABEL, hand-drafted against the PDF. FATF's first report on professional money launderers (PMLs): individuals, organisations (PMLOs) and networks (PMLNs) that launder for a fee or commission on behalf of any criminal client. Describes the three-stage business model (collection, layering through account settlement and proxy structures, hand-back to the client), the roles inside a PML operation, and four dedicated network types: money transport and cash controller networks, money mule networks, digital money and virtual currency networks, and proxy networks of layered shell company accounts moving funds under fictitious contracts. Supporting mechanisms are TBML (phantom shipments, over and under invoicing, BMPE and money brokers), account settlement mechanisms and underground banking including hawala and alternative banking platforms. Section VI covers complicit MVTS providers, bank insiders, lawyers, accountants, TCSPs, payment processors and virtual currency exchangers. Twenty-five case boxes, including the Khanani MLO, Avalanche, PacNet and BTC-e.

Money mules are people who are used to transfer value, either by laundering stolen money or physically transporting goods or other merchandise.
Bank accounts, opened by the mules, serve as the initial layering stage in the laundering process.

All of the victims of these various fraud schemes were instructed to wire money into funnel accounts held by other co-conspirators (money mules), who then quickly transferred the money to other US accounts as well as accounts around the world before victims could discover the fraud.
Proxy networks are PMLs who supply a type of banking service to OCGs, generally through the use of multi-layered transfers via bank accounts.

Funds are moved through a complex chain of accounts established by domestic shell companies under fictitious contracts. The funds from different clients are mixed within the same accounts, which makes it difficult for investigators to trace the funds coming from a particular client.
Funds are returned to the accounts controlled by the initial clients, their close associates or affiliated legal entities and arrangements.
Funds were sent by wire transfer, bank draft or cheque, some of which were then returned to the logistics company.
Most of the funds were transferred out or withdrawn within a few days of receipt, upon instructions of the Nigerian-based OCG.
The funds received in the shell companies' accounts are usually transferred out of the jurisdiction within a few days.
Payment processing companies can be used by criminal organisations to mask transactions and launder the proceeds of crime.

Victims' money, minus PacNet's fees and commission, were made available to the scammers through wire transfers from the PacNet holding account, as well as by PacNet making payments on behalf of the scammers, thereby obscuring the link to the scammers.

The transfer of funds which purport to be related to trade, or to the purchase of goods that are ultimately never shipped or received (also known as "phantom shipments");
ML mechanisms for the layering of illicit proceeds earned in cash commonly include: TBML and fictitious trade, account settlements and underground banking.

Falsifying the number and/or value of goods being shipped to be higher or lower than the corresponding payment, allowing for the transfer or receipt of the value of proceeds of crime (also known as over or under-invoicing);
the PML may resort to other trade-based techniques, such as fake or over invoicing, in order to legitimise the movement of funds between two or more jurisdictions, to balance the system.
PMLs may also create and use false documentation, layer related financial transactions and establish shell and/or shelf companies to facilitate purported trade transactions.
Information received from FINTRAC helped identify a complex TBML where two of the group's central figures hired 10 nominees to establish 25 shell companies.

PML schemes that are arranged with the use of bank accounts consist of multiple layers of shell companies in different jurisdictions, which have been established purely to redistribute and mix funds from various sources.
The number of shell companies and personal bank accounts involved may exceed several thousands.
The term "straw men" refers to informal nominee shareholders and directors who are being controlled by the actual owner or controller of the company.
These actors may also manage a network of registrars who find and recruit nominees (e.g. front men) to register shell companies on behalf of the client
Law enforcement agencies have identified the use of complex corporate structures and offshore vehicles to conceal the ownership and facilitate the movement of criminal proceeds

typologies.label: Account settlement mechanism netting cash against bank balances between criminal clients

citations.quote: A PML may, for example, simultaneously provide ML services to criminals who have cash and want to send funds to bank accounts in other countries, and to criminals who have money in their bank accounts but need cash (e.g. to pay their networks and workers). This modus operandi is called an account settlement mechanism.

Cash controller networks often orchestrate the laundering of the proceeds of crime for multiple OCGs located worldwide through an account settlement system, whereby illicit proceeds are substituted for legitimate funds.

typologies.label: Underground banking, hawala and alternative banking platforms

citations.quote: Underground banking is one tool often used by PMLs. This mechanism is used, with the goal of bypassing the regulated financial sector and creating a parallel system of moving and keeping records of transactions and accountancy.
funds were never actually transferred outside of China to Canada; rather, the value of funds was transferred through an Informal Value Transfer System.
ABPs are a form of shadow banking that make use of bespoke online software to provide banking services, without the regulated and audited customer due diligence checks.

typologies.label: Bulk cash collection and courier transport by cash controller networks

citations.quote: services to transport cash are also being outsourced to specialised cash transportation networks that are responsible for collecting cash, transporting it to pre-determined locations and facilitating its placement in the financial system.
The criminals' modus operandi involved the use of cash couriers traveling by car to pick up dirty cash all over Europe.

typologies.label: Fictitious contracts and false documentation to justify transfers

citations.quote: Funds are transferred abroad under fictitious trade contracts, loan agreements, securities purchase agreements, etc.

these individuals are responsible for either producing or acquiring fraudulent documentation, including fake identification, bank statements and annual account statements, invoices for goods or services, consultancy arrangements, promissory notes and loans, false resumes and reference letters.
Using "consulting services" agreements and other similar types of contracts to create an appearance of legitimacy for illicit wire transfers;

typologies.label: Virtual currency cash-out through straw-man e-wallets, mixers and complicit exchangers

citations.quote: virtual currency is transferred through a complex chain of e-wallets, which may include the use of mixers and tumblers to further enhance the anonymity of the virtual currency transactions.
virtual currency exchangers have been used as unlicensed or unregistered MVTS providers to exchange criminal proceeds in the form of virtual currency to fiat currency.

typologies.label: Black Market Peso Exchange and money brokering of drug proceeds

citations.quote: Using Money (Peso) Brokers, who are third parties that seek to purchase drug proceeds in the location where illicit proceeds are earned by drug cartels (e.g. Colombia, Mexico) at a discounted rate.

Drug traffickers and Colombian cartels are believed to have taken advantage of this currency smuggling network in order to repatriate the proceeds generated in cash through drug sales in Europe back to South America.

typologies.label: Complicit insider and institutional compromise of financial businesses

citations.quote: Criminals will actively seek to recruit complicit insiders within existing institutions or businesses, since these individuals have insider access and may be able to falsify records or initiate transactions in a manner, which bypasses AML/CFT regulations or institutional practices.
The ability of a criminal to purchase or gain ownership or control of a financial business is the ultimate measure of success.

typologies.label: Mirror trading through securities markets to move value abroad

citations.quote: At the same time, two broker companies operating on the London Stock Exchange sold shares for the same price, thus facilitating the transfer of money via mirror trading.

actors.name: Individual professional money launderers
actors.role: Individuals with specialised skills laundering criminal proceeds for a fee or commission, often while in a legitimate professional occupation

citations.quote: An individual PML, who possesses specialised skills or expertise in placing, moving and laundering funds.
those individuals, organisations and networks that are involved in third-party laundering for a fee or commission.

actors.name: Professional money laundering organisations
actors.role: Structured, hierarchical groups of two or more individuals specialising in laundering services for criminals and OCGs

citations.quote: A Professional money laundering organisation (PMLO), which consists of two or more individuals acting as an autonomous, structured group that specialises in providing services or advice to launder money for criminals or other OCGs.

actors.name: Professional money laundering networks
actors.role: Loose, usually global collections of associates and PMLOs that subcontract laundering tasks and share infrastructure

citations.quote: A Professional money laundering network (PMLN), which is a collection of associates or contacts working together to facilitate PML schemes and/or subcontract their services for specific tasks.

actors.name: Cash controller and money transport networks
actors.role: Controllers, collectors and transmitters who receive, pool, transport and hand over bulk cash for multiple OCGs for a processing fee

citations.quote: Criminals and OCGs that generate significant amounts of cash often use the services of cash controller networks that are capable of transferring vast sums of cash on their behalf.

actors.name: Money mule networks
actors.role: Hierarchically controlled networks of recruited account holders, witting or unwitting, used to receive, layer and cash out proceeds, mainly from cybercrime and online fraud

citations.quote: These money mule networks are controlled by a hierarchical structure, and are well-resourced and highly effective in laundering funds.

actors.name: Proxy networks
actors.role: PMLs offering a banking-like service to OCGs through multi-layered transfers across chains of shell company accounts at home and abroad

citations.quote: The main task of these proxy networks is to move client funds to the final, pre-determined destination and to obfuscate the trail of the financial flows.

actors.name: Complicit financial service providers and professional gatekeepers
actors.role: Bankers, MVTS agents, lawyers, accountants, TCSPs, payment processors and exchangers who knowingly or wilfully blindly use their occupation and infrastructure to launder for criminal clients

citations.quote: PMLs may occupy positions within the financial services industry (e.g. bankers and MVTS agents) and DNFBP sectors (e.g. lawyers, accountants and real estate professionals), and use their occupation, business infrastructure and knowledge to facilitate ML for criminal clients.

actors.name: Altaf Khanani Money Laundering Organisation
actors.role: PMLO laundering billions of dollars annually for OCGs, drug trafficking organisations and designated terrorist groups; designated by OFAC in 2015 as a transnational criminal organisation

citations.quote: The Altaf Khanani Money Laundering Organisation (MLO) laundered illicit proceeds for other OCGs, drug trafficking organisations and designated terrorist groups throughout the world.
The Khanani MLO itself was designated by OFAC in 2015 as a "transnational criminal organisation1," pursuant to Executive Order 13581.

actors.name: Altaf Khanani
actors.role: Pakistani national heading the Khanani MLO and Al Zarooni Exchange; moved funds for the Taliban; arrested by the DEA in 2015, pleaded guilty 2016, sentenced to 68 months in 2017

citations.quote: Altaf Khanani, the head of the Khanani MLO and Al Zarooni Exchange, has been involved in the movement of funds for the Taliban

actors.name: Al Zarooni Exchange
actors.role: Exchange house used by the Khanani MLO; designated by OFAC in 2015 alongside the MLO

citations.quote: OFAC designated the exchange house utilised by the Khanani MLO, Al Zarooni Exchange.

actors.name: Avalanche network
actors.role: Malware hosting platform, in operation since at least 2010, running large-scale ML campaigns through country-based money mule networks

citations.quote: Avalanche was a hosting platform composed of a worldwide network of servers that was controlled via a highly organised central system. This cyber network hosted more than two dozen of the world's most pernicious types of malware and several large scale ML campaigns.

actors.name: PacNet
actors.role: Vancouver-based international payment processor and MVTS provider that knowingly processed payments for mail fraud schemes; 12 individuals and 24 entities across 18 countries

citations.quote: PacNet, an international payment processor and MVTS provider based in Vancouver, Canada, helped dozens of fraudsters gain access to US banks.

actors.name: BTC-e
actors.role: Digital currency exchanger operated by a Russian national, indicted in 2017 as an international ML scheme catering to cyber criminals; USD 110 million FinCEN civil penalty

citations.quote: The indictment alleges that BTC-e was an international ML scheme that allegedly catered to criminals, particularly cyber criminals, and evolved into one of the principal means by which criminals around the world laundered the proceeds of their illicit activity.

actors.name: La Cosa Nostra (Palermo)
actors.role: OCG client whose lawyer performed a money box function, laundering proceeds through a Palermo construction company (Operation CICERO)

citations.quote: the boss of a major organised crime group (La Cosa Nostra or LCN) in Palermo, Italy.

extraction_notes: Golden label. Actor classes (PMLs, PMLOs, PMLNs, cash controller, mule and proxy networks, complicit insiders) are categories; anonymised case parties (Subject X, Person A, Person G, J.B.P.C.) and unnamed syndicates (Operation Kandil, the Nigerian syndicate) are not actors; Khanani's terrorist clients are named only in his role. CMI010 not used: the virtual currency content is laundering, not sanctions evasion, so it is emergent under family crypto. Account settlement, underground banking, bulk cash transport, fictitious-contract justification, BMPE and insider compromise have no governed twin and are emergent. Mirror trading (Box 19) is not CM005 Wash Trading; emergent at low. TBML002U rests on one clause inside the over-invoicing sentence and is not labelled; PAT005 and PAT001 rest on one Box 11 sentence and are kept at low as in ADV-2026-0013/0015. Jurisdictions are case locations; fraud victims (the Bahamas, worldwide), the delegation list, meeting venues and the unnamed Country A are excluded.
